# PDFTrail

> PDFTrail is a Mac app (Apple Silicon, macOS 12 or later) that converts PDFs to Excel (.xlsx), Word (.docx), Markdown, JSON and plain text entirely on-device. Born-digital PDFs are read directly from the file's text layer — no OCR guessing; scanned PDFs use on-device OCR. Version 1.3.0 joins tables that run across pages into one table, and after each conversion Table Review shows the pages that need a look, with a grid editor to fix a table and re-export. No account, no sign-up, no cloud uploads. Free to try (10 free Markdown, Word and Excel exports; plain text and JSON unlimited); $24 one-time unlock, no subscription. Mac App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6799649606

## News and engine notes

- [Why PDF to Excel Gets Numbers Wrong, and How to Catch It](https://pdftrail.app/blog/why-pdf-to-excel-numbers-go-wrong/): A pdf to excel wrong numbers slip can hide in a clean column of amounts. Why it happens, and the checks that catch it fast.
- [PDFTrail 1.3: One Table Across Pages and Table Review](https://pdftrail.app/blog/pdftrail-1-3/): PDFTrail 1.3 is on the Mac App Store: tables join across pages, Table Review has a grid editor, scan text is cleaner, and there are three themes.
- [Extract Tables from PDF Without Uploading: Why It Matters](https://pdftrail.app/blog/extract-pdf-tables-without-uploading/): How to extract tables from PDF without uploading it. What "upload" means, which files are safe to send, and the local routes that skip the server.
- [Why a PDF Has No Tables (and How We Find Them Anyway)](https://pdftrail.app/blog/how-pdf-table-extraction-works/): How pdf table extraction works: a PDF stores positioned text and lines, never a table, and the engine rebuilds one before you see it.
- [PDFTrail 1.2: Real Excel Tables from Scanned Pages](https://pdftrail.app/blog/pdftrail-1-2/): Release notes — scanned tables exported with page-true structure, OCR inside embedded images, combined Word export fix, 10 free exports per format.
- [Before and After: Teaching Our Engine to Read Bad Scans](https://pdftrail.app/blog/teaching-the-engine-to-read-bad-scans/): How the engine went from inventing 26 phantom tables on noise pages to zero, the fabrication-never-buys-recall rule, and how Table Review now opens by itself on a page that was partly read or not read.
